noah: Heads up — I see a perf regression on main after the span-mode batching change. nvprof/nsys traces show ~15% higher p95 token latency for redwood-8k-q4, batch=8, seq=512. putting raw numbers and traces below. :frowning_face:

mira: Can you drop the numbers and the commit range? which run configs?

noah: baseline p95 ~120ms/token, after change p95 ~138ms/token (avg token cost up ~12-18% across runs). run command I used:
```
nsys profile -o before --trace=cuda,osrt --capture-range=kernel -- python run_infer.py --model redwood-8k-q4 --batch 8 --seq 512 --iters 200
nsys profile -o after --trace=cuda,osrt --capture-range=kernel -- python run_infer.py --model redwood-8k-q4 --batch 8 --seq 512 --iters 200
```
traces: s3://redwood-traces/perf/1785127/before.qdrep, s3://redwood-traces/perf/1785127/after.qdrep
commit range: good @ abcde1234 -> bad @ f2345de89 (regression introduced between these).

eden: I dug into the nsys timeline: lots more tiny kernel launches clustered around the KV cache refill phase. cuLaunchKernel count up ~2.4x and we see serialization at the host->device enqueue boundary. Looks like the kernel fusion heuristic caused more splitting of fused kernels into small cores that run sequentially. snapshot from trace (annotation):
- before: ~62 kernel launches during forward/kvcache (dominant big GEMM, then ~20 small kernels)
- after: ~148 kernel launches (GEMM still big, but many tiny kv_update/permute kernels show up serially)

patrick: Can we bisect quickly? try `git bisect` with a perf check script.

mira: Suggested bisect steps:
```
git checkout f2345de89 # bad
git bisect start f2345de89 abcde1234
# perf_check.sh should run a short infer with nsys sampling and check p95 or kernel count
./perf_check.sh || git bisect bad
# repeat until commit found
```
I recommend measuring kernel launch counts instead of wall p95 during bisect to reduce noise.

perf-bot: Regression alert — p95 +16% (batch=8,seq=512) on main. Auto-run traces attached: s3://redwood-traces/perf/1785127/after.qdrep. Investigate. :rotating_light:

noah: Ran `git bisect run ./scripts/bisect_kernel_count.sh` — culprit landed at commit 2b9f7a1 (PR #2198) "kernel-selector: enable span fusion heuristic for span-mode". That commit tweaks fusion threshold and a path that now breaks up a previously fused cuda kernel into multiple launches when kv cache is active.

eden: Patch summary from 2b9f7a1: changed heuristic from `if (score > 0.7)` to `if (score >= 0.5)` and introduced a special case for span-mode that splits nodes to avoid oversized kernels. The special case missed accounting for KV cache hot paths, so fusion ends up creating many tiny kernels.

mira: Can we reproduce quickly by toggling an env var? I added a toggle to kernel_selector to disable the new span fusion: `REDWOOD_SPAN_FUSION=0`.

noah: Confirmed. With `REDWOOD_SPAN_FUSION=0` p95 returns to ~121ms and kernel launch count drops back to ~66. Quick commands to test:
```bash
export REDWOOD_SPAN_FUSION=0
python run_infer.py --model redwood-8k-q4 --batch 8 --seq 512 --iters 200
# or set in docker: -e REDWOOD_SPAN_FUSION=0
```

patrick: Nice. That's a safe short-term mitigation. We should revert the heuristic change or refine it to exclude KV cache refill paths.

ci-bot: CI perf job triggered for revert PR. baseline/run metadata: job-7821, seed 20260315.

eden: I compared nsys hotspots: before->after->revert (timeline wall time slices):
- heavy GEMM kernel stable ~45% time
- after: small kernels (kv_update/permute) jumped from 8% -> 28% of time
- revert/disable: small kernels back to ~9%
Total end-to-end p95 delta matches these hotspots. attaching summarized flame chart png (uploaded).

mira: Plan:
1) open revert PR that restores previous threshold + add guard to skip span-fusion if KV cache path detected
2) add a perf test that asserts kernel launch count < 100 for batch=8/seq=512 on our perf CI harness
3) add unit test to kernel_selector to validate fusion decisions for synthetic KV patterns

noah: I'll open the revert PR now and include the nsys artifacts and bisect notes in the PR description. PR #2204 opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/2204 (revert 2b9f7a1 + tests).

patrick: :thumbsup: please also add a small perf note to CHANGELOG and ping infra to re-run extended perf suite.

noah: Will do. Thanks everyone, good triage. I'll keep the thread updated when CI completes and perf diff lands. :eyes:
